justifications.c1: Hardware losses only £500-£2,000 per theft/vandalism (Upper Arley £1,170; Brymbo up to £2,000; GoFundMe ~£1,600) and the Circuit/Cardiff Met data put theft/vandalism at 0.1-0.3% of devices, so expected loss per site per year is far below product cost; the main harm (missed resuscitation) is unquantified.
justifications.c2: Guardian checks are routine and frequent: SCAS checklist sets weekly presence and 'ready' symbol checks (search-confirmed; battery check is actually monthly, misfiled as weekly in the file), GWAA monthly, RCUK checklist; cadence varies by scheme and is guidance, not statute.
justifications.c3: Documented volunteer routine (SCAS, RCUK, parish maintenance policies) and paid managed support (£126-£190/yr); volunteer time is not costed, so labour cost is unquantified.
justifications.c4: Only guidance (RCUK/BHF guardian checklist, ambulance trust instructions, NHS England cabinet guidance); researcher found no statutory duty, insurer condition or liability case.
justifications.c5: Parish councils evidenced holding budget (Clipstone £3,000 earmarked; Kirkby Underwood lease costing; councils paying £135-£190/yr support), but buyers are thousands of small councils acting by minuted resolution; no job advert evidence.
justifications.c6: Community Heartbeat Trust (with Rotaid connected cabinets) and Duchy Defibrillators (monitored cabinet, £190+VAT monitoring fee in Delabole PC paper) already bundle monitoring for this exact site type, though they are also competitors.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay proven (CHT support fees, Duchy £190 monitoring, Turtle DefibMonitor subscription search-confirmed, Rotaid licence), but Turtle/Rotaid/Duchy already sense temperature, door and presence; the AED-status-light/Circuit-sync gap is unverified either way.
justifications.c8: Retrofit cabinet monitors already ship (Turtle, SaveStation) so sensing is proven; optical reading of varied AED status LEDs is somewhat custom; no BOM, battery or certification evidence searched.
justifications.c9: Ongoing readiness logging on The Circuit plus contractual annual support (CHT adoption agreement 'at least £126 per annum'; Redlingfield £540/4 yrs search-confirmed; Duchy £190+VAT) ≥£100/site/yr; record duty is guidance/contract, not statute.
justifications.c10: Many local news reports of unreturned AEDs (Cheltenham, Dereham, Bath, Barnsley, Coventry, Cannock), RCUK/AACE 'Check Your Defib Week' campaign and academic poster; no forum/complaint source and theft concern is partly debunked by the same data.

weakest: The money at stake per site is tiny (theft/vandalism 0.1-0.3% of devices, £500-£2,000 hardware) and UK incumbents already sell cabinet monitoring with temperature, door and presence sensing.
